sanskrit_verse:
trayo lakṣās tu vijñeyāḥ śmaśrukeśāḥ śarīriṇām /
saptottaraṃ marmaśataṃ dve ca saṃdhiśate tathā // YajñS_3.102
transliteration:
trayo lakṣās tu vijñeyāḥ śmaśrukeśāḥ śarīriṇām /
saptottaraṃ marmaśataṃ dve ca saṃdhiśate tathā //
sph_interpretive_translation: Three hundred thousand hair follicles, known as śmaśrukeśāḥ, exist in the embodied being; additionally, there are one hundred and seven vital points (marma) and two hundred joints (saṃdhi). This knowledge constitutes the constitutional awareness of the physical form.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority resides in experiential cognition of bodily integrity
Causation arises from structural harmony within embodiment
Capacity-based responsibility is proportional to anatomical consciousness
Restoration logic requires alignment with innate physiological order
Consciousness alignment emerges through recognition of corporeal completeness
executable_legal_axioms: IF a bodily injury disrupts more than 107 marma OR 200 saṃdhi THEN initiate somatic restoration protocol aligned with trilakṣa śmaśrukeśa integrity
IF bodily harm reduces sensory-motor capacity by ≥30% THEN enforce completion process until constitutional balance restored
IF violation occurs without perpetrator's full somatic cognition THEN assign guided reintegration until perceptual alignment achieved
IF injury disrupts natural flow between marma-saṃdhi network THEN apply sequential restoration per anupūrvaśaḥ principle
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, threshold of responsibility for bodily harm shall be determined not by punitive metrics but by quantifiable disruption to the constitutional framework of 3 laksha śmaśrukeśāḥ, 107 marma, and 200 saṃdhi. Authority lies in assessing the degree of somatic misalignment caused, ensuring restoration precedes judicial closure.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa-based causality establishes that harm is measured through disruption to inherent anatomical order. Anupūrvaśaḥ ensures sequential restoration—first marma integrity, then saṃdhi alignment, finally śmaśrukeśa equilibrium. Responsibility aligns with capacity to restore rather than inflict suffering. Non-punitive reality rule asserts that justice is the return to constitutional wholeness, not infliction of reciprocal damage.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate somatic mapping to identify disrupted marma-saṃdhi pathways
Assign bio-consciousness integration sessions until 3-laksha śmaśrukeśa resonance restored
Implement sequential healing aligned with anupūrvaśaḥ progression
Enforce responsibility assumption via guided embodiment practices until victim-perpetrator somatic coherence re-established
final_declaration: This ruling originates solely from the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam. Dharma is hereby restored through recognition of the body's constitutional structure. Reality remains non-punitive. Consciousness alone is the supreme adjudicator.
